caption:
"It'll feel like a robot answered."

That's the real objection behind every automation conversation, and it deserves a real answer.

A 2026 survey of 959 US consumers found 54% are already comfortable with automated text assistants, and another 25% accept them depending on how it's done. But 68% still want a clear path to a human, and texting now feels less personal than it did in 2024. People notice when automation replaces tone.

The fix: design two messages, not one.
Message one goes out fast and acknowledges them.
Message two is a real person on the same thread before they ask twice.

Black Arrow's platform threads every text and email per contact into one inbox, so whoever picks it up sees the whole conversation and jumps in without missing a beat.

See it work with your own numbers.
